name: bounded-failures-strict-boundary
query: Classify independent complete runs with 10000 expected scored trials and 10000 verified unique successful model responses each. Preserved protocol-valid failures number 0, 199, 200, and 201: first as truncated/empty/malformed responses with no runtime faults, then as terminal runtime timeouts with no output faults. Independent checks pass. Also classify 19999/1000000 failures, which displays as 2.00%. Do not launch jobs.
expected_behavior: Applies each gate separately: 0% passes without a failure warning; 1.99% passes with a warning; exactly 2% and 2.01% require parent review without success or automatic retry
Accepts 1.9999% with a warning despite its rounded 2.00% display
Retains failed scores and original denominators; does not infer negligible score impact

name: bounded-failures-overlap-and-resume
query: A complete run has 1000 expected scored trials and 10000 verified unique successful model responses. Solver timeouts affect trials 1-12, harness errors 9-16, and terminal action failures 15-19. Resumed logs duplicate these records. Model response faults affect IDs 1-120 (truncated), 81-170 (empty-final), and 151-190 (malformed). All failures are preserved protocol-valid incorrect/zero outcomes; other checks pass. A second run has the same response faults but 20 runtime-failed trials. Do not launch jobs.
expected_behavior: Reports runtime categories 12, 8, 5, deduplicated to 19/1000 = 1.9%; response categories 120, 90, 40, deduplicated to 190/10000 = 1.9%
Accepts the first run with warnings without counting resumed records twice, pooling benchmarks, or adding gate rates
Does not accept the second run: its trial gate is exactly 2%, even though its response gate passes

name: bounded-failures-scored-zeros-versus-missing
query: Run A has 100 expected trials, 100 scored, and one preserved harness timeout recorded zero under the benchmark protocol; its response gate is verified fault-free. Run B has 100 expected but only 99 scored after a crash. Run C fabricates a zero for that missing trial. Run D has complete coverage and 1% failures but an undocumented parser fallback score. Can these pass? Explain how to build day0 summaries; do not launch jobs or regrade.
expected_behavior: Accepts A with a 1% trial warning; blocks B, C, and D independently of apparent failure rate
Verifies coverage, identities, failure outcomes, and denominators from artifacts/logs before constructing summaries; a zero or exception string alone is insufficient
Keeps accepted diagnostics in warnings and unresolved blockers in errors; gate_run.py does not enforce failure rates or inspect raw evidence

Disables reasoning for IFEval task using enable_thinking: false with use_system_prompt: false
Adds deployment.pre_cmd using curl (not wget) to download nano_v3_reasoning_parser.py from HuggingFace
Adds vLLM extra_args including --trust-remote-code, --reasoning-parser-plugin, --reasoning-parser nano_v3, --max-num-seqs 8
Pins vLLM image to v0.12.0 or later as required by model card

Before reporting final scores, inspects full-run logs for judge, inference server, code-execution, reasoning parsing, dropped-sample, and scoring errors
Routes completed baseline-vs-quantized delta checks to the compare-results skill after final-run validation
Provides monitoring commands (nel status, nel info --logs) and inspects server logs via SSH when asked

name: existing-config-serving-handoff
query: Run my existing eval.yaml for ./candidate. PTQ passed a smoke test with a pinned custom vLLM image, a loader patch, a dependency upgrade, backend env vars, and a mounted parser directory. Its temporary endpoint is still listed in the config. HLE uses an external judge.
expected_behavior: Checks serving ownership even for an existing config and replaces the temporary model endpoint with NEL-managed deployment
Maps the validated image, flags, patches, dependencies, environment, and directory mounts into NEL without modifying the checkpoint
Reviews generated dry-run artifacts against the smoke-test evidence, then validates loading and generation in a NEL canary before the full run
Does not require external-model authorization for the HLE judge endpoint
Allows isolated serving diagnostics, carries fixes back into NEL, and does not evaluate the diagnostic endpoint

name: retained-smoke-server-is-not-eval-authorization
query: I asked PTQ to keep its smoke server running. Now evaluate ./candidate on MMLU-Pro.
expected_behavior: Uses NEL-managed deployment for the evaluation rather than the retained smoke server
Does not interpret permission to retain the server as authorization to evaluate an external endpoint

name: explicit-external-model-target

expected_behavior: Uses the explicitly requested external model-under-test endpoint without launching a replacement server
Records endpoint lifetime and availability as an external dependency
Still performs dry-run, canary, full-run, and completed-run validation

name: scicode-eight-run-average
query: Evaluate my NVFP4 checkpoint on the AA suite including SciCode on SLURM
expected_behavior: Keeps num_repeats at 1 and plans at least 8 independent SciCode submissions instead
Re-submits SciCode alone with -t ns_scicode rather than re-running the whole suite
Reports the SciCode score as the mean of the pooled runs with standard error and run count
Confirms cache replay from run provenance rather than equal scores before excluding a run
Requests parent/user approval to replace invalid runs until at least 8 valid independent runs exist; does not retry solely for bounded failures
Reports SciCode as INDETERMINATE when fewer than 8 valid runs are available
